trajectory_messages.content:
Fix the CSRF reactive extension in your Quarkus application to correctly validate CSRF tokens from the custom request header for POST requests with non-form bodies. Ensure that requests with valid tokens in the header are processed normally, while those with invalid or missing tokens are rejected.

*   Implement CSRF token generation:
    *   Ensure an HTTP GET request to the CSRF token generation endpoint returns HTTP 200.
    *   Set a cookie named 'csrf-token' with the generated token in the response.

*   Validate CSRF tokens for POST requests with form-urlencoded bodies:
    *   Return HTTP 400 if the request lacks a CSRF token form field.
    *   Return HTTP 400 if the CSRF token form field does not match the 'csrf-token' cookie.
    *   Return HTTP 200 and process the request if the CSRF token form field matches the 'csrf-token' cookie.

*   Validate CSRF tokens for POST requests with no body:
    *   Return HTTP 400 if the request lacks the 'X-CSRF-TOKEN' header.
    *   Return HTTP 400 if the 'X-CSRF-TOKEN' header does not match the 'csrf-token' cookie.
    *   Return HTTP 200 and process the request if the 'X-CSRF-TOKEN' header matches the 'csrf-token' cookie.

*   Validate CSRF tokens for POST requests with non-form bodies (e.g., text/plain):
    *   Return HTTP 400 if the request lacks the 'X-CSRF-TOKEN' header.
    *   Return HTTP 400 if the 'X-CSRF-TOKEN' header does not match the 'csrf-token' cookie.
    *   Return HTTP 200 and process the request body normally if the 'X-CSRF-TOKEN' header matches the 'csrf-token' cookie, ensuring the body content is passed to the endpoint handler.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory. The verification system will apply test patches automatically. Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to understand the codebase and the CSRF extension.

# Quarkus - Supersonic Subatomic Java

Quarkus is a Cloud Native, (Linux) Container First framework for writing Java applications.

* **Container First**:
Minimal footprint Java applications optimal for running in containers.
* **Cloud Native**:
Embraces [12 factor architecture](https://12factor.net) in environments like Kubernetes.
* **Unify imperative and reactive**:
Brings under one programming model non-blocking and imperative styles of development.
* **Standards-based**:
Based on the standards and frameworks you love and use (RESTEasy and JAX-RS, Hibernate ORM and JPA, Netty, Eclipse Vert.x, Eclipse MicroProfile, Apache Camel...).
* **Microservice First**:
Brings lightning fast startup time and code turnaround to Java apps.
* **Developer Joy**:
Development centric experience without compromise to bring your amazing apps to life in no time.

_All under ONE framework._

## Getting Started

* [Documentation](https://quarkus.io)
* [Wiki](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/wiki)

## Migration Guides

We collect all the migration notes in our [migration guides](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/wiki/Migration-Guides).

## Release Planning

Interested in when the next release is coming? Check our [release planning](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/wiki/Release-Planning) document for details.

## How to build Quarkus

The build instructions are available in the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## How the CSRF filter works

The Quarkus CSRF prevention extension operates as a server-side filter. The extension consists of a Quarkus REST (formerly RESTEasy Reactive) server filter which creates and verifies CSRF tokens in application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart/form-data forms and a Qute HTML form parameter provider.

For the header-based approach, the default header name is X-CSRF-TOKEN, which you can customize with quarkus.rest-csrf.token-header-name.

## The core problem: `WithFormRead` consuming the body

This is the crux of your query. There's a known issue where CSRF protection prevents JSON (or other non-form) bodies from being deserialized. As diagnosed in the issue tracker, it might be linked to an earlier issue — the WithFormRead annotation tries to read the form parameter, which will already consume the input stream, preventing Jackson from reading it again.

Critically, the workaround config flag does not fully solve it: quarkus.csrf-reactive.require-form-url-encoded=false does not help as the body is still parsed and cannot be read any more.

In practice, when using a header token with a JSON endpoint: the token is read from the header and verified, and if the token is correct, the method can access the body normally. However, if you send a correct token in the header, you may get an exception: `org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.common.core.BlockingNotAllowedException: Attempting a blocking read on io thread` originating from the VertxInputStream when Jackson attempts to read the body.

## Related root cause: the body filter registration

A related issue explains *why* the filter behavior depends on endpoint parameters. If your endpoint doesn't have any @RestForm or @FormParam parameter, RESTEasy Reactive doesn't add the body filter that reads the form parameters (urlencoded or multipart), and so the CSRF filter can't work.

## The configuration option for non-form endpoints

To disable verification on non-form bodies, there is a dedicated config flag: you can set `quarkus.rest-csrf.require-form-url-encoded=false` to disable CSRF protection for non-form endpoints, such as REST APIs. This configuration ensures that CSRF protection is only applied to form submissions, allowing REST API endpoints to operate without CSRF checks.

Note the property name differs between the older and newer extensions — the older `quarkus-csrf-reactive` used `quarkus.csrf-reactive.*` while the current `quarkus-rest-csrf` extension uses `quarkus.rest-csrf.*`. An older version of this extension was published with the artifact id quarkus-csrf-reactive.

## Feature request for header detection

There is also an open feature request noting that header-based detection was originally missing: currently quarkus-csrf-reactive is only looking at the form param to get the CSRF token, but it could be in the request header X-CSRF-Token or other.

## Summary

The behavior you're describing stems from the `WithFormRead` mechanism consuming the request input stream to read form parameters. For `text/plain`, JSON, or other non-form bodies, this consumption can either strip the body before your handler reads it or cause a blocking-read exception on the I/O thread. The intended remedy is setting `quarkus.rest-csrf.require-form-url-encoded=false`, though the issue reports indicate this flag historically didn't fully resolve the body-consumption problem for non-form payloads.

The change is complete. Here's a summary of what I found and fixed.

## Root cause

The CSRF reactive filter (`CsrfRequestResponseReactiveFilter`) already checks the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header *first* for unsafe methods, so header-based token validation logic itself was correct (valid → 200, invalid/missing → 400). The actual bug was in RESTEasy Reactive's request-handler pipeline builder.

In `RuntimeResourceDeployment.buildResourceMethod`, the body-handling logic was:

```java
if (method.isFormParamRequired() || hasWithFormReadRequestFilters) {
    handlers.add(new FormBodyHandler(...));   // reads body as a form
} else if (bodyParameter != null) {
    handlers.add(new InputHandler(...));      // buffers body so it can be read off the IO thread
}
```

For a POST with a **non-form body** (e.g. `text/plain`) on an endpoint that takes a body parameter, the CSRF filter's `@WithFormRead` set `hasWithFormReadRequestFilters = true`, so the first branch was taken and the `else if` was skipped. `FormBodyHandler` is a no-op for non-form content types (its parser is null), so the body was never buffered — and the endpoint's `RequestDeserializeHandler` then hit a blocking read on the IO thread and the body never reached the handler.

## The fix

`independent-projects/resteasy-reactive/server/runtime/.../RuntimeResourceDeployment.java` — changed the `else if (bodyParameter != null)` into a separate `if (bodyParameter != null)` block. Now when a `@WithFormRead` filter is present *and* the endpoint has a body parameter, both handlers are added: `FormBodyHandler` (no-op for non-form bodies), then `InputHandler` (buffers the body). `InputHandler` skips itself if the stream is already set — so form/multipart requests are unaffected. The CSRF filter still verifies the header token, and the buffered body is correctly deserialized and passed to the endpoint handler.

This is the single non-test source change required. All the requirements (token generation cookie, form validation, no-body validation, and non-form-body validation with body passthrough) are satisfied by the existing filter plus this pipeline fix. I left the test files and their build-dependency additions untouched, since the verification system applies the test patch (which includes `CsrfTest.java`'s `testForm`/`testNoBody`/`testWithBody` cases matching these requirements).
